    StartersThe soupLinguini spilled it. Remy fixed itHow to make it2 leeks, sliced40g butter2 potatoes, diced1 L chicken stock100ml thickened cream1 small bunch chives, snippedwhite pepper, to tasteSweat the leeks in the butter over low heat until soft.Add the potatoes and stock and simmer until the potato is very tender.Blend silky smooth with the cream and season.Serve topped with chives and white pepper. Anyone can cook.Mushroom and cheeseToasted on the chimney by lightningHow to make it8 Swiss brown mushrooms120g gruyere, grated1 small bunch thyme, leaves picked1 garlic clove, crushed1 tbsp extra virgin olive oilRemove the mushroom stems.Mix the gruyere with the thyme and garlic and fill the caps.Drizzle with oil and roast at 220°C until bubbling.Rest a few minutes before serving.Bread, with a proper crustListen for the crackleHow to make it2 baguettes100g salted butter, at room temperature200g sliced leg ham200g ripe brieTake the salted butter out of the fridge so it is soft at room temperature.Warm the baguettes in a 200°C oven for 6 minutes until the crust crackles when you squeeze it.Split each baguette lengthways and spread thickly with the butter.Fill with folds of the ham and slices of brie, close and cut into short lengths to share.MainsRatatouille, layered fineThe dish that takes Ego straight back to his mum's kitchenHow to make it1 red capsicum, diced1 brown onion, diced2 garlic cloves5 tomatoes2 zucchinis1 eggplant2 yellow squashes1 small bunch thyme4 tbsp extra virgin olive oilCook the capsicum, onion, garlic and 2 chopped tomatoes into a soft sauce and spread it in a baking dish.Slice the zucchini, eggplant, squash and remaining tomatoes thin and layer them in a spiral over the sauce.Drizzle with thyme infused oil and cover with baking paper.Bake covered at 140°C until completely tender.Rest briefly before serving.Sweetbreads à la GusteauThe old recipe Linguini was told to cook. Remy rewrote itHow to make it600g veal sweetbreadssalt, to taste2 tbsp plain flour50g butter180ml chicken stock1 tsp lemon juiceSoak the veal sweetbreads in cold water in the fridge for 2 hours.Simmer the sweetbreads in salted water for 4 minutes, then plunge into iced water and peel off the membrane.Press the sweetbreads under a weighted tray in the fridge for an hour.Slice into 2cm pieces, season with salt, dust with the flour and pan-fry in 30g of the butter for 3 minutes a side until golden.Deglaze the pan with the chicken stock and lemon juice, reduce by half, then swirl in the remaining 20g cold butter and spoon the sauce over the sweetbreads.SweetsColette's crème brûléeColette teaches, Remy tugs Linguini's hairHow to make it500ml thickened cream1 vanilla bean6 egg yolks100g caster sugar, plus extra for the topsHeat the oven to 150°C. Split the vanilla bean, scrape the seeds into the cream and warm it with the pod until it just steams.Whisk the yolks and 100g caster sugar until pale, then pour in the warm cream slowly, whisking, and strain into a jug.Pour into 4 ramekins in a baking dish, fill the dish with hot water halfway up the ramekins and bake until set with a slight wobble.Cool, then chill at least 3 hours.Sprinkle each top with a thin layer of caster sugar and torch, or grill close to the element, until it cracks like glass.DrinksA good BordeauxEgo's order. Any good Bordeaux will do at homeHow to make it100g blackberries4 thyme sprigs, plus extra to serve1 tbsp honey600ml red grape juice1 lemon, half juiced330ml sparkling water1 bag iceLightly crush the blackberries with the thyme and honey in a jug.Add the grape juice and lemon juice and stir.Chill for 30 minutes (included in cook time), then strain.Pour into wine glasses over ice, top with sparkling water and garnish with thyme and a blackberry.
